The Ti–45Al–8Nb–0.2C alloy was produced by vacuum arc melting at the GfE Metalle und Materialien (Germany) in the form of extruded rods with dimensions of ∅48 × 90 mm
The cast material was subjected to quasi-isothermal hot extrusion in a shell at Т = 1250°C with the degree of deformation of 7 : 1
annealing at Т = 1280°C for 2 h
cooling in a furnace to 900°С at a rate of ≈1 K/s
aging at this temperature for 3 h

The fact that the strength remains unchanged with increasing temperature in the cast Ti–43.7Al–3.2(Nb,Cr,Mo)–0.2B alloy is explained by the presence of a lamellar structure with a high number density of coherent and semicoherent γ/α2 boundaries, in which the processes of absorption of lattice dislocations is complicated
These processes occur more intensely in the alloy with a duplex structure owing to the presence of a fine globular structure

The deformation is delocalized due to the absorption of lattice dislocations by grain boundaries, grain-boundary sliding, the enhanced nucleation of lattice and twinning dislocations, and the activation of cross slip and dislocation climbing.
